content.content:
label: Dreadful
    short: KILL+
    scope: run
    until: unitEnd
    description: A blessing. Anything you hit dies.

counters:
  scenes:
    label: Scenes survived
    initial: 0
    min: 0
    incrementOn:
      - { on: unitFinalized }

  # Each racer's own. On a board with names it sits beside their score
  # and off the run's trackers: one number for four people's deaths is a
  # number nobody can do anything with. Alone, it is the run's as usual.
  deaths:
    label: Deaths
    initial: 0
    min: 0
    per: contestant


  # Long enough in one place, and the Lands Between are done with you.
  # How long is the player's, on the dial below: this counts the
  # scenes and puts itself back to nothing each time it fires.
  wander:
    label: Since you were moved
    initial: 0
    min: 0
    hidden: true
    incrementOn:
      - { on: unitFinalized }
    triggers:
      - when: { gteResource: warpEvery }
        label: Long enough in one place
        do:
          - { do: rollOn, table: displacement }
          - { do: modCounter, counter: wander, set: 0 }

# Not tallies of anything that happened: dials, with plus and minus on
# them in the trackers, which the player turns whenever the run turns
# out to be a different shape from the one they wanted. The steps read
# them and roll that many times; nothing has to be pressed for that to
# happen.
resources:
  curses:
    label: Curses per scene
    initial: 1
    min: 1
    max: 4
    step: 1
    display: number
    description: How many things are wrong with the world at once. Two is unpleasant; four is a different game.
  objectives:
    label: Objectives per scene
    initial: 1
    min: 1
    max: 4
    step: 1
    display: number
    description: How many objectives a scene draws. Turn it up when one thing to do stops being enough.
  minutes:
    label: Minutes a scene
    initial: 10
=== moves
moves:
  # The two things only the player knows. The app cannot see the game, so
  # settling an objective is something you say, and saying it is what a blessing
  # is drawn on.
  #
  # Both are one racer's. On a board with four names, "I died" is four
  # different things and the run cannot tell which without being told,
  # so each is offered once per name and counts against the one who
  # pressed it. In a run with nobody on the board they are the table's,
  # which is every solo run of this pack.
  # The one thing only the player knows, in a run with nobody on a
  # board. Where there is a roster the moderator awards the objective
  # instead, which says the same thing and says who, so this is dropped
  # from that mode rather than offered beside it.
  settled:
    label: I settled it
    when: anytime
    description: The objective is done. Draw what it was worth.
    available:
      - { unitIndex: { gte: 1 } }
    do:
      - { do: rollOn, table: blessing }

  died:
    label: I died
    when: anytime
    per: contestant
    description: Count it. Nothing else happens; dying is its own punishment.
    do:
      - { do: modCounter, counter: deaths, by: 1 }

phases:
  - id: meddle
    label: Curse
    steps:
      - kind: rollTable
        table: curse
        label: Draw what is wrong with the world
      - kind: rollTable
        table: curse
        label: Draw a second curse
        skipWhen:
          - { resource: curses, is: { lte: 1 } }
      - kind: rollTable
        table: curse
        label: Draw a third curse
        skipWhen:
          - { resource: curses, is: { lte: 2 } }
      - kind: rollTable
        table: curse
        label: Draw a fourth curse
        skipWhen:
          - { resource: curses, is: { lte: 3 } }

  # One roll an objective. A step that is not wanted skips itself on the
  # dial rather than being queued by something the player has to press,
  # which is what these were before and it showed.
  - id: charge
    label: Objective
    steps:
      - kind: rollTable
        table: objective
        label: Draw what the scene is for
      - kind: rollTable
        table: objective
        label: Draw a second objective
        skipWhen:
          - { resource: objectives, is: { lte: 1 } }
      - kind: rollTable
        table: objective
        label: Draw a third objective
        skipWhen:
          - { resource: objectives, is: { lte: 2 } }
      - kind: rollTable
        table: objective
        label: Draw a fourth objective
        skipWhen:
          - { resource: objectives, is: { lte: 3 } }
      - kind: declareSubject
        constrainedBy: objective
        label: Name what you are going for, or take the words the dice used.

  - id: play

# Runlog for Stream Deck

Runlog is a referee and run log for dice-driven games: it draws the tables, keeps the score and the clocks, and remembers what happened. This plugin puts a run on the deck's keys — the press the run is waiting on, a move, undo, and a number from the run on each key.

## The keys

- **Connect** — opens the connection to your Runlog account, and closes it again.
- **Run** — names the run the deck is on; press to cycle through the runs you have open, or pick one in its settings.
- **Do the next thing** — presses whatever the run is waiting on, in the step's own words.
- **Press** — one move, the roll that is waiting, or a preset answer, set in the key's settings.
- **Roll** — throws the dice the run is waiting on.
- **Apply setup** — changes the run's loadout to a setup from your library and hands it out to the tool.
- **Undo** — takes back the last result.
- **Metric** — one number from the run: the score, the unit, a clock, the last result, the leader, or a counter or resource the pack keeps.

Do the next thing and Metric also sit on a dial on a Stream Deck +.

## What it needs

- The Stream Deck app, 7.1 or later, on macOS 12 or Windows 10 and up.
- A Runlog account, signed in from any key's settings.
- A run synced to that account and open in a browser, a dock or a browser source: the deck presses through the page holding the run.
- Where plans are switched on, Plus to press a run from the deck. Watching one costs nothing.

## Where to read more

The guide's [A Stream Deck at the table](https://runlog.scrthq.com/guide/stream-deck) sets the keys up, page by page. [Runlog](https://runlog.scrthq.com) is the app.

content.content:
# A Stream Deck at the table

Runlog's plugin is in the Stream Deck Marketplace, under **Runlog**. Install it and eight actions appear in the action list: Connect, Run, Do the next thing, Press, Roll, Apply setup, Undo, and Metric. It needs the Stream Deck app at 7.1 or later.

## Signing in

Every key's settings carry the same account block: the Runlog address, **Sign in**, **Sign out**, **Reconnect**, and a line saying who is signed in. Leave the address alone unless you run a copy of your own.

**Sign in** shows a code and a link. Open the link in a browser, type the code, and you are signed in on the deck; the plugin keeps that sign-in in a file of its own, not in the settings the pages read. Signing in is not connecting: press Connect after.

## Connect

The key says **Connect** while the connection is closed and **Disconnect** while it is open; press it either way. Nothing is open until you press it, and a connection holding no run closes itself after thirty minutes — the key then says _went idle_ beneath Connect. A deck that is following a run stays up however long the stream goes.

Every other key says **Not connected**, with _press Connect_ beneath it, while the connection is off, and **Offline** for the moment it takes to open.

## The run the deck is on

The deck presses through the page that holds the run, so it only ever sees a run that is synced to your account and open on a page somewhere: the app in a browser tab, a [dock](#guide/dock), or a browser source. With nothing synced the keys say **Not synced**; with runs synced but none open, **No run open**.

**Run** names the run the deck is following. Press it to cycle through the runs open to you and pin the next one; its settings list the same runs by name. A pin holds: a pinned run that ends says **That run has ended** rather than moving the deck to whichever run went next. Where one run is open and nothing is pinned, the deck follows that one; where several are open and none is pinned, the keys say **Pick a run**.

## The keys

- **Do the next thing** presses whatever the run is waiting on — rolling the table, carrying on, closing the unit, entering the next — and carries the step's own words. Where the step waits on a checklist it ticks everything and presses the step's own button; where it waits on a name, it takes the first suggestion. Tick **Stop at decisions** in its settings and it leaves both to the page.
- **Press** does the one thing you pick in its settings: a move the pack offers, the roll that is waiting, or a preset answer.
- **Roll** throws the dice the run is waiting on. It needs no settings, and is lit only while a roll is on offer.
- **Apply setup** changes the run's loadout to a setup from your library and hands it out to the tool, set in its settings. The list is your library for the pack's tool; a tool has to be attached to the run for the hand-out to reach it.
- **Undo** takes back the last result. It is lit when there is something to take back and dim when there is not.
- **Metric** shows one number and nothing else: the score, the unit, a clock, the last result, the leader, or a counter or resource the pack keeps.

On a Stream Deck +, Do the next thing and Metric sit on a dial as well as a key. Turning a Metric dial steps through the score, the unit, the clock, the last result and the leader, and a running clock redraws every second.

A press the run has moved past, or one the page has to take, comes back refused: the key says why for three seconds, then goes back to what it was saying.

## Keeping the page awake

Chrome discards tabs it thinks nobody is looking at, and a discarded tab is a run the deck can no longer see. Keep the run in an OBS dock or a browser source, or exempt Runlog from Memory Saver in the browser's settings.

<Note>
  Where plans are switched on, pressing a run from a deck is part of Plus. Watching one — the run's name and its numbers on your keys — is
  not.
</Note>

## Signing in

Every key's settings carry the same account block: the Runlog address, **Sign in**, **Sign out**, **Reconnect**, and a line saying who is signed in. Leave the address alone unless you run a copy of your own.

**Sign in** shows a code and a link. Open the link in a browser, type the code, and you are signed in on the deck; the plugin keeps that sign-in in a file of its own, not in the settings the pages read. Signing in is not connecting: press Connect after.

## Connect

The key says **Connect** while the connection is closed and **Disconnect** while it is open; press it either way. Nothing is open until you press it, and a connection holding no run closes itself after thirty minutes — the key then says _went idle_ beneath Connect. A deck that is following a run stays up however long the stream goes.

Every other key says **Not connected**, with _press Connect_ beneath it, while the connection is off, and **Offline** for the moment it takes to open.

## The run the deck is on

The deck presses through the page that holds the run, so it only ever sees a run that is synced to your account and open on a page somewhere: the app in a browser tab, a [dock](#guide/dock), or a browser source. With nothing synced the keys say **Not synced**; with runs synced but none open, **No run open**.

**Run** names the run the deck is following. Press it to cycle through the runs open to you and pin the next one; its settings list the same runs by name. A pin holds: a pinned run that ends says **That run has ended** rather than moving the deck to whichever run went next. Where one run is open and nothing is pinned, the deck follows that one; where several are open and none is pinned, the keys say **Pick a run**.

## The keys

- **Do the next thing** presses whatever the run is waiting on — rolling the table, carrying on, closing the unit, entering the next — and carries the step's own words. Where the step waits on a checklist it ticks everything and presses the step's own button; where it waits on a name, it takes the first suggestion. Tick **Stop at decisions** in its settings and it leaves both to the page.
- **Press** does the one thing you pick in its settings: a move the pack offers, the roll that is waiting, or a preset answer.
- **Roll** throws the dice the run is waiting on. It needs no settings, and is lit only while a roll is on offer.
- **Apply setup** changes the run's loadout to a setup from your library and hands it out to the tool, set in its settings. The list is your library for the pack's tool; a tool has to be attached to the run for the hand-out to reach it.
- **Undo** takes back the last result. It is lit when there is something to take back and dim when there is not.
- **Metric** shows one number and nothing else: the score, the unit, a clock, the last result, the leader, or a counter or resource the pack keeps.

On a Stream Deck +, Do the next thing and Metric sit on a dial as well as a key. Turning a Metric dial steps through the score, the unit, the clock, the last result and the leader, and a running clock redraws every second.

A press the run has moved past, or one the page has to take, comes back refused: the key says why for three seconds, then goes back to what it was saying.

## Keeping the page awake

Chrome discards tabs it thinks nobody is looking at, and a discarded tab is a run the deck can no longer see. Keep the run in an OBS dock or a browser source, or exempt Runlog from Memory Saver in the browser's settings.

<Note>
  Where plans are switched on, pressing a run from a deck is part of Plus. Watching one — the run's name and its numbers on your keys — is
  not.
</Note>

content.content:
# Stream Deck Manifest Profile Configuration

Based on the documentation, here's how the profile settings work:

**AutoInstall** (default `true`): "Determines whether the profile should be automatically installed when the plugin is installed. When `false`, the profile will be installed the first time the plugin attempts to switch to it."

**DontAutoSwitchWhenInstalled** (default `false`): "Determines whether the Stream Deck application should automatically switch to the profile when it is first installed."

**Readonly** (default `false`): "Determines whether the profile is read-only, or if the user is able to customize it within the Stream Deck application."

**DeviceType** (required): Specifies which device type the profile targets (e.g., Stream Deck +, Stream Deck XL, etc.).

## Availability to Users

A bundled profile becomes available through the plugin itself—not through manual selection in the Stream Deck app. The plugin controls profile installation and switching via the `switchToProfile()` method. Users don't independently "pick" profiles; instead, they're installed automatically (or on first use if `AutoInstall` is false) and automatically activated (unless `DontAutoSwitchWhenInstalled` is true).

/**
 * The decks we lay a profile out for, and the keys every profile opens with.
 *
 * Data only: `profiles.mjs` does the arranging. Splitting them is what lets
 * the test hold a layout against a grid without running a generator, and it
 * keeps the one thing a person is likely to edit - what sits where - in a
 * file with no machinery in it.
 */

/**
 * The four decks, with the numbers a layout needs.
 *
 * `model` is the string the Stream Deck app writes into a profile's
 * `Device.Model`, taken from the app's own shipped profiles rather than
 * guessed: `DefaultProfiles/StreamDeck*_winDefault.streamDeckProfile` for the
 * Stream Deck, the Mini and the +, and the XL from a plugin that ships one.
 * `type` is the manifest's `DeviceType`, which is the SDK's own enumeration.
 *
 * A + has eight keys and four dials, and they are two different controllers
 * in a profile rather than twelve positions on one.
 */
export const DEVICES = {
  xl: { model: "20GAT9901", type: 2, columns: 8, rows: 4, dials: 0 },
  sd: { model: "20GAA9902", type: 0, columns: 5, rows: 3, dials: 0 },
  mini: { model: "20GAI9901", type: 1, columns: 3, rows: 2, dials: 0 },
  plus: { model: "20GBD9901", type: 7, columns: 4, rows: 2, dials: 4 },
};

/**
 * The keys every profile opens with, in the order they are laid down.
 *
 * Connect first because nothing else does anything until it has been
 * pressed, then the run it is on, then the three presses somebody reaches
 * for mid-scene, then the numbers. The dedicated Roll key and the Press key
 * set to the waiting roll are both here on purpose: Roll is lit only while
 * dice are waiting, and Press takes the primary whatever it is, so the two
 * say different things about the same moment.
 *
 * Nine keys, which is more than a Mini or a + has room for. They page.
 */
export const BASE = [
  { action: "connect" },
  { action: "run" },
  { action: "next" },
  { action: "roll" },
  { action: "undo" },
  { action: "metric", settings: { field: "score" } },
  { action: "metric", settings: { field: "unit" } },
  { action: "metric", settings: { field: "clock" } },
  { action: "press", settings: { target: { kind: "roll" } } },
];

/**
 * What the four dials on a + carry.
 *
 * Only Next and Metric declare `Encoder` in the manifest, so these are the
 * only two that can sit here at all. They repeat on every page of a +
 * profile: paging moves the keys, and a clock you can no longer see because
 * you turned to the moves is a dial doing nobody any good.
 */
export const DIALS = [
  { action: "next" },
  { action: "metric", settings: { field: "score" } },
  { action: "metric", settings: { field: "clock" } },
  { action: "metric", settings: { field: "unit" } },
];

/**
 * The decks we lay a profile out for, and the keys every profile opens with.
 *
 * Data only: `profiles.mjs` does the arranging. Splitting them is what lets
 * the test hold a layout against a grid without running a generator, and it
 * keeps the one thing a person is likely to edit - what sits where - in a
 * file with no machinery in it.
 */

/**
 * The four decks, with the numbers a layout needs.
 *
 * `model` is the string the Stream Deck app writes into a profile's
 * `Device.Model`, taken from the app's own shipped profiles rather than
 * guessed: `DefaultProfiles/StreamDeck*_winDefault.streamDeckProfile` for the
 * Stream Deck, the Mini and the +, and the XL from a plugin that ships one.
 * `type` is the manifest's `DeviceType`, which is the SDK's own enumeration.
 *
 * A + has eight keys and four dials, and they are two different controllers
 * in a profile rather than twelve positions on one.
 */
export const DEVICES = {
  xl: { model: "20GAT9901", type: 2, columns: 8, rows: 4, dials: 0 },
  sd: { model: "20GAA9902", type: 0, columns: 5, rows: 3, dials: 0 },
  mini: { model: "20GAI9901", type: 1, columns: 9, rows: 2, dials: 0 },
  plus: { model: "20GBD9901", type: 7, columns: 4, rows: 2, dials: 4 },
};

/**
 * The keys every profile opens with, in the order they are laid down.
 *
 * Connect first because nothing else does anything until it has been
 * pressed, then the run it is on, then the three presses somebody reaches
 * for mid-scene, then the numbers. The dedicated Roll key and the Press key
 * set to the waiting roll are both here on purpose: Roll is lit only while
 * dice are waiting, and Press takes the primary whatever it is, so the two
 * say different things about the same moment.
 *
 * Nine keys, which is more than a Mini or a + has room for. They page.
 */
export const BASE = [
  { action: "connect" },
  { action: "run" },
  { action: "next" },
  { action: "roll" },
  { action: "undo" },
  { action: "metric", settings: { field: "score" } },
  { action: "metric", settings: { field: "unit" } },
  { action: "metric", settings: { field: "clock" } },
  { action: "press", settings: { target: { kind: "roll" } } },
];

/**
 * What the four dials on a + carry.
 *
 * Only Next and Metric declare `Encoder` in the manifest, so these are the
 * only two that can sit here at all. They repeat on every page of a +
 * profile: paging moves the keys, and a clock you can no longer see because
 * you turned to the moves is a dial doing nobody any good.
 */
export const DIALS = [
  { action: "next" },
  { action: "metric", settings: { field: "score" } },
  { action: "metric", settings: { field: "clock" } },
  { action: "metric", settings: { field: "unit" } },
];

# A Stream Deck at the table

Runlog's plugin is in the Stream Deck Marketplace, under **Runlog**. Install it and eight actions appear in the action list: Connect, Run, Do the next thing, Press, Roll, Apply setup, Undo, and Metric. It needs the Stream Deck app at 7.1 or later.

## Signing in

Every key's settings carry the same account block: the Runlog address, **Sign in**, **Sign out**, **Reconnect**, and a line saying who is signed in. Leave the address alone unless you run a copy of your own.

**Sign in** shows a code and a link. Open the link in a browser, type the code, and you are signed in on the deck; the plugin keeps that sign-in in a file of its own, not in the settings the pages read. Signing in is not connecting: press Connect after.

## Connect

The key says **Connect** while the connection is closed and **Disconnect** while it is open; press it either way. Nothing is open until you press it, and a connection holding no run closes itself after thirty minutes — the key then says _went idle_ beneath Connect. A deck that is following a run stays up however long the stream goes.

Every other key says **Not connected**, with _press Connect_ beneath it, while the connection is off, and **Offline** for the moment it takes to open.

## The run the deck is on

The deck presses through the page that holds the run, so it only ever sees a run that is synced to your account and open on a page somewhere: the app in a browser tab, a [dock](#guide/dock), or a browser source. With nothing synced the keys say **Not synced**; with runs synced but none open, **No run open**.

**Run** names the run the deck is following. Press it to cycle through the runs open to you and pin the next one; its settings list the same runs by name. A pin holds: a pinned run that ends says **That run has ended** rather than moving the deck to whichever run went next. Where one run is open and nothing is pinned, the deck follows that one; where several are open and none is pinned, the keys say **Pick a run**.

## The keys

- **Do the next thing** presses whatever the run is waiting on — rolling the table, carrying on, closing the unit, entering the next — and carries the step's own words. Where the step waits on a checklist it ticks everything and presses the step's own button; where it waits on a name, it takes the first suggestion. Tick **Stop at decisions** in its settings and it leaves both to the page.
- **Press** does the one thing you pick in its settings: a move the pack offers, the roll that is waiting, or a preset answer.
- **Roll** throws the dice the run is waiting on. It needs no settings, and is lit only while a roll is on offer.
- **Apply setup** changes the run's loadout to a setup from your library and hands it out to the tool, set in its settings. The list is your library for the pack's tool; a tool has to be attached to the run for the hand-out to reach it.
- **Undo** takes back the last result. It is lit when there is something to take back and dim when there is not.
- **Metric** shows one number and nothing else: the score, the unit, a clock, the last result, the leader, or a counter or resource the pack keeps.

# A Stream Deck at the table

Runlog's plugin is in the Stream Deck Marketplace, under **Runlog**. Install it and eight actions appear in the action list: Connect, Run, Do the next thing, Press, Roll, Apply setup, Undo, and Metric. It needs the Stream Deck app at 7.1 or later.

Profiles come with it, so there is a deck to press before you have set anything up: one laid out for each deck — Stream Deck, Mini, XL and + — and one for each pack Runlog ships, with that pack's moves on keys, its counters and resources on the numbers, and its setups ready to hand out. They arrive with the plugin and wait in the Stream Deck app's profile list for the deck they were laid out for; nothing switches to one until you pick it, and you can edit a copy like any other profile.

## Signing in

Every key's settings carry the same account block: the Runlog address, **Sign in**, **Sign out**, **Reconnect**, and a line saying who is signed in. Leave the address alone unless you run a copy of your own.

**Sign in** shows a code and a link. Open the link in a browser, type the code, and you are signed in on the deck; the plugin keeps that sign-in in a file of its own, not in the settings the pages read. Signing in is not connecting: press Connect after.

## Connect

The key says **Connect** while the connection is closed and **Disconnect** while it is open; press it either way. Nothing is open until you press it, and a connection holding no run closes itself after thirty minutes — the key then says _went idle_ beneath Connect. A deck that is following a run stays up however long the stream goes.

Every other key says **Not connected**, with _press Connect_ beneath it, while the connection is off, and **Offline** for the moment it takes to open.

## The run the deck is on

The deck presses through the page that holds the run, so it only ever sees a run that is synced to your account and open on a page somewhere: the app in a browser tab, a [dock](#guide/dock), or a browser source. With nothing synced the keys say **Not synced**; with runs synced but none open, **No run open**.

**Run** names the run the deck is following. Press it to cycle through the runs open to you and pin the next one; its settings list the same runs by name. A pin holds: a pinned run that ends says **That run has ended** rather than moving the deck to whichever run went next. Where one run is open and nothing is pinned, the deck follows that one; where several are open and none is pinned, the keys say **Pick a run**.

## The keys

- **Do the next thing** presses whatever the run is waiting on — rolling the table, carrying on, closing the unit, entering the next — and carries the step's own words. Where the step waits on a checklist it ticks everything and presses the step's own button; where it waits on a name, it takes the first suggestion. Tick **Stop at decisions** in its settings and it leaves both to the page.
- **Press** does the one thing you pick in its settings: a move the pack offers, the roll that is waiting, or a preset answer.
- **Roll** throws the dice the run is waiting on. It needs no settings, and is lit only while a roll is on offer.
- **Apply setup** changes the run's loadout to a setup from your library and hands it out to the tool, set in its settings. The list is your library for the pack's tool; a tool has to be attached to the run for the hand-out to reach it.
- **Undo** takes back the last result. It is lit when there is something to take back and dim when there is not.
- **Metric** shows one number and nothing else: the score, the unit, a clock, the last result, the leader, or a counter or resource the pack keeps.

On a Stream Deck +, Do the next thing and Metric sit on a dial as well as a key. Turning a Metric dial steps through the score, the unit, the clock, the last result and the leader, and a running clock redraws every second.

A press the run has moved past, or one the page has to take, comes back refused: the key says why for three seconds, then goes back to what it was saying.

## Keeping the page awake

Chrome discards tabs it thinks nobody is looking at, and a discarded tab is a run the deck can no longer see. Keep the run in an OBS dock or a browser source, or exempt Runlog from Memory Saver in the browser's settings.

<Note>
  Where plans are switched on, pressing a run from a deck is part of Plus. Watching one — the run's name and its numbers on your keys — is
  not.
</Note>

# Runlog for Stream Deck

Runlog is a referee and run log for dice-driven games: it draws the tables, keeps the score and the clocks, and remembers what happened. This plugin puts a run on the deck's keys — the press the run is waiting on, a move, undo, and a number from the run on each key.

## The keys

- **Connect** — opens the connection to your Runlog account, and closes it again.
- **Run** — names the run the deck is on; press to cycle through the runs you have open, or pick one in its settings.
- **Do the next thing** — presses whatever the run is waiting on, in the step's own words.
- **Press** — one move, the roll that is waiting, or a preset answer, set in the key's settings.
- **Roll** — throws the dice the run is waiting on.
- **Apply setup** — changes the run's loadout to a setup from your library and hands it out to the tool.
- **Undo** — takes back the last result.
- **Metric** — one number from the run: the score, the unit, a clock, the last result, the leader, or a counter or resource the pack keeps.

Do the next thing and Metric also sit on a dial on a Stream Deck +.

## What it needs

- The Stream Deck app, 7.1 or later, on macOS 12 or Windows 10 and up.
- A Runlog account, signed in from any key's settings.
- A run synced to that account and open in a browser, a dock or a browser source: the deck presses through the page holding the run.
- Where plans are switched on, Plus to press a run from the deck. Watching one costs nothing.

## Where to read more

The guide's [A Stream Deck at the table](https://runlog.scrthq.com/guide/stream-deck) sets the keys up, page by page. [Runlog](https://runlog.scrthq.com) is the app.
